Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Threema. It sends Threema messages from your Gladys scenes, with your
own **Threema Gateway** account. Send only: Gladys does not read the answers.

> This integration has never been tested with a real Threema Gateway account: it follows the official API
> documentation. Feedback is welcome.

## What you need

- A **Threema Gateway ID in basic mode**, created on [gateway.threema.ch](https://gateway.threema.ch/en/):
  8 characters starting with `*`, with its **API secret**.
- Threema Gateway **credits**: every message sent uses some; they are bought from Threema.

**Basic mode**: the Threema Gateway server holds the private key of your ID and prepares each message for the
recipient itself. It is the simplest mode to set up; if you want the key to stay with you, this connector does
not fit (end-to-end mode not supported).

## Configuration

| Field                                  | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gateway ID                             | `*XXXXXXX`, 8 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| API secret                             | Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to Threema.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Allowed recipients                     | Up to 20, separated by commas: Threema IDs (8 characters), phone numbers in international format (`+41…` or `0041…`) or e-mail addresses linked to a Threema account. **The only** recipients this connector ever sends to (scene action, test button, and the "My account" recipients of users); the first one is the default. |
| Messages per hour, at most             | 20 by default, from 1 to 500.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Also send the Gladys messages of users | Off by default (see below).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Buttons:

- **Check the account**: asks Threema for the credits left. Free, nothing sent, not counted in the limit.
- **Send a test message**: a short message to an allowed recipient (the first one when empty). Costs credits and
  counts in the limit.

## Scene action "Send a Threema message"

- **Text**: may hold scene variables. Beyond 3,500 bytes (the Threema limit), it is cut and ends with "…".
- **Recipient** (optional): one of the allowed recipients, written as you like (`alice123`,
  `+41 79 123 45 67`); empty, the first one of the list. A recipient outside the list is refused, even when it
  comes from a scene variable: nothing is sent.
- **Output**: `message_id`, the message ID given by Threema (empty when it could not be read).

## Gladys messages to users (option)

This connector is also a Gladys message channel. When the administrator turns on **"Also send the Gladys
messages of users"**, a user who enters their Threema recipient in "My account" receives through Threema the
messages Gladys sends them, **only if this recipient is also in the allowed recipients** of the configuration
(any user can fill "My account"; a recipient outside the list gets nothing, the logs and the status say so,
masked). What goes through, each one costing credits and counting in the same hourly limit:

- the core "Send a message" scene action (to every channel, or to Threema only);
- the answers of the core "Ask the AI" scene action, when the scene picks no channel or picks Threema;
- the Gladys system messages to **every administrator**: Gladys upgraded (at the next start), backup failure,
  Gladys Plus subscription, weekly digest, low batteries. The **system message channel** setting of Gladys can
  keep them out of Threema.

Gladys waits 5 s for a channel to answer: the connector answers 3.5 s after the message came in at most (even
while its configuration or `/data` is still being read), and the send goes on behind (15 s at most for the
request); its outcome, failure included, goes to the logs.

## What protects your account

- **Nothing leaves by itself**: not at start, not at a reconnection, not on a timer; only a scene action, a
  click on "Send a test message", or a Gladys message when the option is on and its recipient is allowed.
- **No duplicate**: a message is never sent again. When Threema does not answer in time or the connection is
  cut, the message may have left: the error says so, and it is not sent again.
- **Hourly limit**: counted before the send, over a sliding hour, kept in `/data` (a restart does not reset
  it). A message refused by Threema (400, 401, 402, 404, 413, 429) does not count; a server error (5xx), a
  timeout or a cut connection does. When `/data` is unreadable, read-only or slow, the send does not wait
  (1 s at most) and the status warns that the limit only holds until the next restart.
- **One message at a time**, 10 waiting at most, the others refused.
- **Refused ID or secret** (401): nothing more sent with them (an 8-bit fingerprint, never the secret, kept in
  `/data`) until they change or a button succeeds.
- **Pause** after a 429 or a server error: 60 s, doubled each time up to 1 h, or the delay Threema asks up to
  6 h; buttons included, kept across a restart.
- **No credits left** (402): the status says so; nothing was sent.
- The secret, the text of the messages and whole recipients never appear in the logs, the status or `/data`:
  an ID becomes `AL******`, a number `+…67`, an address `j…@…`.

## Statuses

"Ready" as long as nothing was sent (the ID and the secret are only checked at the first message or with the
"Check the account" button); "Threema Gateway answered" after a success; otherwise the reason: refusal, pause,
limit reached, no credits, network.

## Privacy

The messages go through the Threema servers (Switzerland). What Threema does with them falls under the terms of
its Gateway service.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Threema asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Threema Gateway account | `section` | No | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Threema. It needs a Threema Gateway ID in basic mode, created on gateway.threema.ch. In basic mode the Gateway server holds the private key of this ID and prepares each message for the recipient itself. Every message costs credits, bought from Threema. Send only: Gladys cannot read the answers. Nothing leaves without a scene action or a click on a button, and never more than the hourly limit below. |
| Gateway ID | `string` | Yes | The Gateway ID in basic mode: 8 characters starting with *. |
| API secret | `secret` | Yes | The API secret of this ID (gateway.threema.ch, your ID). Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to Threema. |
| Allowed recipients | `string` | No | The only recipients this integration ever sends to, separated by commas (20 at most): Threema IDs (8 characters), phone numbers in international format (+41…) or e-mail addresses linked to a Threema account. The first one is used when a scene names none. A user's “My account” recipient must be in this list too. |
| Messages per hour, at most | `number` | No | Beyond it, nothing is sent until the oldest message of the last hour is an hour old (from 1 to 500). Every path counts: scenes, buttons and forwarded Gladys messages. |
| Also send the Gladys messages of users | `boolean` | No | Off by default. On: the messages Gladys sends to a user whose “My account” recipient is in the allowed list go through Threema too, each one costing credits: the core “Send a message” and “Ask the AI” scene actions, and the Gladys system messages to administrators (upgrade at the next start, backup failure, Gladys Plus, weekly digest, low batteries) unless the system message channel setting of Gladys keeps them elsewhere. |

## How to install Threema in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Threema appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-threema:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-threema](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-threema).

Threema requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Threema is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
